title: Group Therapy and Aury - Blended Care Intervention Study
summary:
The aim of the study is to investigate a combination treatment
consisting of group therapy over five sessions and the use of the
use of the virtual counselor Aury. After a detailed diagnosis, the study participants are randomly assigned to the waiting group or the intervention group. On the one hand, the intervention consists of group therapy over five sessions of 100 minutes each covering the topics of sleep, anxiety, worry and rumination, depression and resources. As a second part of the intervention, the virtual counselor Aury will be used between sessions to help deepen the content and implement it in everyday life. At the end of the five-week intervention and after a further three months, the study participants will be sent questionnaires to assess changes following the intervention. There is no intervention in the waiting group; the participants also complete questionnaires after five weeks and three months.

interventions.name:
intervention group
Study participants in the intervention group take part in transdiagnostic group therapy over five weekly sessions of 100 minutes each and use a chatbot between sessions to better consolidate the contents of the therapy. When using the chatbot, study participants can decide for th

waiting control group 
Study participants in the waiting control group wait a total of 17 weeks (5 weeks during the intervention + 12 weeks until follow-up) and can also participate in the intervention (transdiagnostic group + chatbot) after completing all surveys.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Ability to consent
-German-speaking
-Psychopathology: Scores ≥ 10 on at least one subscale (Depression, Anxiety, Somatization) of the Patient Health Questionnaire – D (PHQ-D), or a score >10 on the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI).
Exclusion criteria:
- Psychopathology: Indication for inpatient treatment (acute psychosis, suspected danger to self or others, substance dependence
self-harm or danger to others, substance dependence (F1X.2), serious psychopathology), clinical impression of inadequately treated borderline personality disorder, pronounced personality disorders which, according to clinical impression limits group ability
- No willingness to participate in group therapy
- No willingness to use the digital chatbot
- No willingness to participate in the study in case of randomized allocation to the waiting control group
- Start of guideline psychotherapy (excluding probationary sessions) in the intervention period
